title: Washing your hands with little water
summary: The first barrier against diarrhoea and infections.
steps: Wash your hands before eating, cooking or giving care, and after using the toilet.
“Tippy tap” system: a hanging container with a small hole, tipped with your foot, saves a lot of water.
Lather for 20 seconds: palms, backs, between the fingers, nails.
Without water: hand sanitiser (except on very dirty hands).

title: Toilets without running water
summary: Prevent sewage from contaminating water and food.
steps: In a flat: empty the water from the bowl and line it with two strong bin bags.
After each use, cover with a little sawdust, cat litter, dry soil or ash to limit smells and flies.
Tie the bags closed and store them outdoors in a closed bin.
Outdoors: dig a hole 15 to 20 cm deep, at least 60 metres from any water source, and fill it in.
warnings: Do not flush if the sewers are out of service (risk of backflow).

title: Diarrhoea and dehydration
summary: Rehydrate above all, especially children and the elderly.
steps: Drink often, in small sips.
Homemade rehydration solution (WHO): 1 litre of safe water + 6 level teaspoons of sugar + 1/2 level teaspoon of salt.
Keep eating light food (rice, banana, bread) as soon as possible.
Seek urgent care for blood in the stools, high fever, or signs of severe dehydration (drowsiness, no urine).
warnings: Follow the salt and sugar doses exactly: a solution that is too salty is dangerous.
Oral rehydration salts (ORS) sachets from the pharmacy are better: keep some in your kit.

title: Managing stress and fear
summary: Keeping a cool head is the first survival skill.
steps: Stop: don't act in a rush.
Box breathing: breathe in for 4 seconds, hold for 4, breathe out for 4, hold for 4; repeat 4 times.
Observe: assess the situation, the dangers and your resources.
Plan: a short list of priorities (see the rule of 3), then act step by step.
Keep a routine (meals, sleep, tasks) and give everyone a role, children included.
Talk, stay together, limit exposure to anxiety-inducing news.

title: Managing waste without collection
steps: Sort: food waste on one side, dry packaging on the other.
Tie food-waste bags tightly and store them outdoors, in a closed bin, in the shade.
Rinse and flatten packaging to reduce volume and smells.
Compost or bury peelings if a garden is available, away from water sources.
